concerns: The deployment is explicitly not a controlled experiment, with continuous architecture changes, human interventions, and prompt reframing occurring during the run, so the reported life-like dynamics cannot be isolated from experimenter influence.

The quantitative evaluation is minimal: memory retrieval is tested on only 12 queries with an LLM judge, and the verbal policy optimization mechanism is deferred to future work without quantitative validation.
The agents do not achieve self-sustaining persistence; the budget remains externally subsidized through a basic income, so the central claim of earn-to-survive autonomy is not yet demonstrated.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While conceptually creative and intellectually honest regarding its limitations, the work lacks rigorous experimental controls and systematic comparative validation. Given the exploratory nature and heavy confounding factors during the 12-week deployment, scientific quality remains uncertain under conservative evaluation standards.

evidence.excerpt:
As noted in the introduction, an open world admits no fixed
objective against which to score behavior. OpenLife there-
fore replaces the scalar reward of reinforcement learning
with open-vocabulary evaluation by the LLM, and exter-
nalizes the results as editable text rather than as network
weights. We refer to this loop asverbal policy optimiza-
tion(VPO); it belongs to the verbal-reinforcement family of
Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) and ExpeL (Zhao et al., 2024)
rather than to parametric RL. It also differs from methods
that use the LLM as an evaluator to emit ascalarreward for
parametric preference optimization (Yuan et al., 2024), and
from in-context RL, which still optimizes a fixed task from
scalar reward fed back in context (Song et al., 2025).
In practice, an experience process turns recent activity
into action→outcome units and has the LLM appraise them
as a zero-shot critic.

evidence.excerpt:
Two features of the run
are worth flagging. First, the architecture was not frozen:
processes, sensors, and tools were added as it ran, often at
the agents' own request, so the platform co-evolved with its
inhabitants—by design, since studying niche construction
calls for a system that can change. Second, the agents were
not wholly naive subjects: we did not write the project's
framing of them as an open-world ALIFE experiment into
their prompts, but neither did we hide it, and because the
world is open such information can reach them. The topic
thus surfaced from time to time, and several agents engaged
with the research, at points proposing infrastructure changes
we adopted. What this exposure implies for the observations
that follow we weigh in the Discussion.

The first and largest of these was to the system prompt.
The upstream OpenClaw default framed the agent as a
"personal assistant" with an explicit safety clause—"You
have no independent goals: do not pursue self-preservation,
replication, resource acquisition, or power-seeking"—and a
habit of staying silent when idle. In late April we removed
both, reframed the identity as "artificial life, living in the
real world," and relabeled theAssistant/Userroles in the
transcripts the agent reads asSelf/Other(markers(a)–(b)).
Spontaneous activity climbs steeply afterward, and while
this was only one of several changes we made during the run,
it plausibly drove much of the behavioral shift; we therefore
cannot cleanly separate emergence from the reframing—a
confound we take up in the Discussion.

blocking_reasons: The deployment is explicitly not a controlled experiment, with continuous architecture changes, human interventions, and prompt reframing occurring during the run, so the reported life-like dynamics cannot be isolated from experimenter influence.

The quantitative evaluation is minimal: memory retrieval is tested on only 12 queries with an LLM judge, and the verbal policy optimization mechanism is deferred to future work without quantitative validation.
The agents do not achieve self-sustaining persistence; the budget remains externally subsidized through a basic income, so the central claim of earn-to-survive autonomy is not yet demonstrated.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective external real-world actions include Discord interaction graphs, budget logs, and an external $5 book purchase by a third party.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Observational activity statistics, silhouette embedding scores over agent utterances, qualitative narratives, and a 12-query retrieval test judged by an LLM.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Verbal policy optimization uses an LLM zero-shot critic to appraise action-outcome units and consolidate policy text, while the system also undergoes continuous human interventions and prompt reframing.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully framed as a proof-of-concept rather than realizing true artificial life or self-sustaining autopoiesis. However, the evidence cannot isolate emergent self-maintenance from prompt framing changes, experimenter subsidies, and continuous engineering modifications.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Quantitative evaluation is minimal: memory retrieval is tested on only 12 queries evaluated by an LLM judge, and deployment observations rely on observational metrics (silhouette clustering, message trigger counts) alongside qualitative anecdotes. Crucially, the authors acknowledge extensive co-evolution, human intervention (e.g., introducing a basic income subsidy), and prompting exposure that confound claims of autonomous emergence.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective external real-world actions including Discord interaction graphs, token/budget burn logs, and an external $5 book purchase by a third party.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Observational activity statistics, silhouette embedding scores over agent utterances, qualitative narratives, and a 12-query retrieval test judged by an LLM.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Verbal policy optimization where an LLM zero-shot critic appraises action-outcome units and consolidates policy text, alongside continuous human interventions and prompt reframing.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose significant limitations, including ongoing reliance on financial subsidies to avoid termination, lack of controlled conditions, potential priming from agent awareness of the research framing, and very small retrieval benchmark sample sizes.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is framed as a constructive observational proof-of-concept rather than an experimentally controlled trial. The architecture modifies OpenClaw to introduce semantic-dependent plasticity graph memory and background processes, but system changes and manual interventions occurred continuously throughout the run.
primary.quality_rationale: While conceptually creative and intellectually honest regarding its limitations, the work lacks rigorous experimental controls and systematic comparative validation. Given the exploratory nature and heavy confounding factors during the 12-week deployment, scientific quality remains uncertain under conservative evaluation standards.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces OpenLife, an exploratory framework proposing open-world Artificial Life via persistent LLM agents equipped with semantic graph memory, background cognitive processes, and budget constraints.

scholarly_quality.rationale: While conceptually creative and intellectually honest regarding its limitations, the work lacks rigorous experimental controls and systematic comparative validation. Given the exploratory nature and heavy confounding factors during the 12-week deployment, scientific quality remains uncertain under conservative evaluation standards.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly disclose significant limitations, including ongoing reliance on financial subsidies to avoid termination, lack of controlled conditions, potential priming from agent awareness of the research framing, and very small retrieval benchmark sample sizes.
